News.title: Nigel Farage secures record £36m donation from crypto billionaire to help give Reform ‘fair fight’ at the polls
News.content:
NIGEL Farage has secured a record £36million donation from a crypto billionaire in order to help give Reform a “fair fight” in the polls.

It is the largest single donation to a British political party.



Brit Ben Delo, co-founder of trading platform BitMEX, insisted only a huge cash injection would allow the party to battle against the “entrenched advantages” enjoyed by its political rivals.

Mr Delo, who was already Reform UK’s second largest donor, wrote in The Daily Telegraph: “My conclusion from Reform’s recent troubles is that they should spend less time trying to raise funds to compete on equal terms and more time preparing for government.”



The significant sum dwarfs the previous donation record of £10million, left to the Conservatives as a bequest.

Mr Farage, who faces an ongoing police probe into party financing, said: “I am honoured and humbled that Ben Delo has shown such confidence in Reform.



“Ben knows that we are the only party that can turn the country around and reverse Britain’s decline.”

Mr Delo is now Reform’s largest donor having previously been second behind billionaire Christopher Harborne, who gave £9million to the party last year.

Last year, he was given an unconditional pardon by US President Donald Trump over a Bank Secrecy Act violation.

Mr Delo said in his article: “Unlike the people who express mock concern for the health of ‘our democracy’ while doing everything they can to keep it as a cartel, I want a fair fight and a level playing field.



“My conclusion from Reform’s recent troubles is that they should spend less time trying to raise funds to compete on equal terms and more time preparing for government.”

The Telegraph reported the £36million figure represents £1million a month between now and the latest possibly date of the next general election in 2029, but Mr Delo has made the payment up front to avoid attempts to block it.

MPs last week backed measures including a cap on overseas donations at £100,000 and a suspension of funding through cryptocurrency, but the draft legislation still needs to be passed by the House of Lords to become law.

Ministers have argued the changes will prevent foreign money influencing elections, but Reform has said it is a bid to choke its funding.

Reform has faced ongoing questions about its finances which overshadowed its annual conference last week following an undercover investigation broadcast on Channel 4 News.



Detectives from the Metropolitan Police are investigating after the report showed senior party figures appearing to discuss how to disguise donations from foreign sources.

Reform UK denies any wrongdoing and has said it will co-operate fully with the probe.

Mr Farage’s long-time aide Dan Jukes, who denies wrongdoing, and head of policy James Orr have been suspended pending an internal investigation into the allegations.

The party leader also faces an investigation by Parliament’s standards watchdog over a £5 million gift he received from Mr Harborne.

Mr Farage has said he has done nothing wrong and the gift was not political.



A Labour spokesperson said: “Nigel Farage is still up to his neck in scandal over his secret £5million ‘gift’ from his other crypto-billionaire backer and the criminal investigation into potentially illegal donations.

“The questions he faces aren’t going away – in fact they’re piling up.

“Reform UK can’t buy their way out of questions about sleaze, criminal mates and dodgy finances.

“It’s time Farage and Reform finally came clean with the public, co-operated fully with the police, and proved they’re not just in it for themselves.”

Liberal Democrat Cabinet Office spokesperson Lisa Smart said: “Nigel Farage wants to bring Trump’s America to our shores by buying his way into power.

“He’s trying to get into Number 10 as if it’s a stop on a monopoly board.

“It can’t go on like this. Andy Burnham needs to introduce a cap on political donations. Our democracy depends on it.”

News.title: Two women, 27 & 41, brutally attack man, 70, during dog walk by kicking and stamping on OAP as pair jailed
News.content:
'TERRIFYING ORDEAL' Two women, 27 & 41, brutally attack man, 70, during dog walk by kicking and stamping on OAP as pair jailed

TWO women who brutally attacked a 70-year-old man by kicking and stamping on him while he was on a dog walk have been jailed.

Leanne Yates, 41, and Chloe Thompson, 27, subjected the victim to a “terrifying ordeal” in a Middlesbrough park.



The pair broke away from the group they were with and approached the pensioner on the evening of March 9 to ask him for money.

He said he had none and took his dog home, Teeside Crown Court heard.



When he returned to Ayresome Gardens to walk his other dog he came across the group again.

The victim moved out of the way to let them pass but CCTV shows the man in the group “strike the pensioner to his face” Cainan Lonsdale, prosecuting, said.



The pensioner punched back only for the man to “make another blow to his face” knocking him to the ground.

Thompson is then seen dragging the victim onto the pavement from the grass verge while Yates “is stamping and kicking him” as the group gathered around, the barrister said.

The victim’s pockets were rifled through and his satchel was taken, but later discarded when the gang found it only held a dog lead, bags, a hat and gloves.

The pensioner went home and his partner took him to hospital after seeing his injuries.



He said his “vision was affected” and photos showed bruising, swelling and a large cut on his cheek.

The women were both found with drugs when they were arrested.

Yates, of no fixed address, pleaded guilty to attempted robbery; assault occasioning actual bodily harm; and the possession of a class A drug.

Thompson, of New Street in Thornaby, admitted attempted robbery; assault occasioning actual bodily harm; two counts of the possession of a class C drug; and failing to surrender.

Judge Richard Wright acknowledged the difficult backgrounds of the two women and considered their upbringings mitigating circumstances.



He told the pair at the sentencing hearing: “Yates – you took the lead in kicking and stamping on him.

“Thompson – you dragged him about. This was a terrifying ordeal for him.”

“When you attack a 70 year old man, in the dark, who was doing no more than walking his dog.

“When you put him to the ground and kick and stamp on him – you go to prison” he said.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Thompson and Yates were jailed for three years and three years and nine months respectively.

News.title: Woman suffered seizure after being repeatedly raped in secluded park by man, 25, she met in nightclub
News.content:
'RUINED MY LIFE' Woman suffered seizure after being repeatedly raped in secluded park by man, 25, she met in nightclub

A WOMAN suffered a seizure after being repeatedly raped in a secluded park by a man she had met in a nightclub.

The victim had been out with pals in South Shields and ended up in Industry nightclub before being separated from friends and meeting Aiden Johnson, 25.

They kissed and swapped details before leaving the club together at around 5am when the woman said she needed to get a taxi home.

Johnson offered to help get her one as he led her through a housing estate, which prosecutors said was “on the pretext of finding a taxi”.





He then attempted to lift her dress up but she told him she wasn’t interested in having sex with him.

Newcastle Crown Court was told he then led her to a park where she stumbled to the floor.

Prosecutor Ben Sayers said Johnson then “seized the opportunity” to carry out the first part of the sex attack.

Mr Sayers told the court: “Ignoring her resistance, he continued to subject her to further sexual acts. She repeatedly told him to stop.”



He raped her three times in total as well as sexually assaulting her.

Mr Sayers said: “She told him throughout she did not want to do anything. He ignored her protests and her efforts to push and kick him off. He tried to reassure her it was all fine.”

During the brutal attack, the woman suffered a seizure and when she came round she told Johnson she had been sexually abused once and didn’t need it again.

Johnson told her, he “wasn’t like that”.



He left in a taxi and asked her to go with him but she refused.

She called her family and later reported the attack.

When he was arrested, Johnson claimed he went to the park hoping for sex but said none occurred.

However, his DNA was found on her underwear.

The woman said in a victim impact statement: “What happened to me has completely ruined my life.



“I haven’t been the same person since and don’t think I ever will be.

“The trauma got so bad I took myself to a bridge to end my life.

“I’ve been diagnosed with PTSD.

“I think about what happened from the minute I wake up until I go to sleep. I can’t switch off. I have constant nightmares.

“I’ve tried all the support there is but still feel broken. I most likely will be on medication for the rest of my life so I can feel somewhat human and have some control of my body.



“I’m scared to be alone in public in case something like this happens again.

“I didn’t do anything wrong. I trusted someone to help me get home and they used that trust to hurt me, so I don’t trust anyone.

“This has taken everything from me, my confidence, my mental health, sense of safety and my trust.

“It’s hard to put into words how much this has destroyed me.”

Johnson, who has a caution for sexual assault when he was a youth, was found guilty of three counts of rape, attempted rape and assault by penetration.



He was imprisoned for eight years and has been put on the sex offenders register for life and was also given a restraining order.

Judge Sarah Mallett told him: “Your conduct that night has devastated her life as it has your own.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Defending Johnson, Jane Foley said Johnson continues to maintain the sexual activity was consensual and has a supportive family.

The court was told he had led a “productive life”.

News.title: Why the fate of Trump’s final two years in office hangs in the balance – as JD and Lil’ Marco battle to succeed him
News.content:
DONALD TRUMP used to say he was “tired of winning” but has finally admitted: “I’m getting a little bit tired of politics now.”

After a near two-hour turn on Wednesday evening, the ageing President was back in front of 10,000 true believers on Thursday night.



Half an hour into his planned ten-minute closing remarks of the Republican Party’s jazzy gathering in Dallas, Texas, The Don was in pensive mode.

He had just seen what we all witnessed in the giant arena: Life after him.



Mocked by the Mad Mullahs of Iran, battered in the opinion polls back home and facing the prospect of being a lame duck come November, this impromptu convention to launch his party’s midterm election campaign felt a little like a last hurrah.

“Just pretend I’m on the ballot”, Trump begged two nights in a row, as he sought to breathe life into his party’s tricky prospects for crucial Senate and Congressional elections eight weeks away.



The fate of his final two years in office hangs in the balance. If he retains his grip on Washington, he has promised the world — in the form of a $5,000 bung to every US citizen.

Should he lose, it will be a long 24 months cornered in the West Wing as his Democrat enemies use every tool in the shed to push and probe his legacy, family and businesses.

Six months into his “four to six week” war in the Middle East, Trump still insists his party must stick with him for a similar bounce to 2016 and 2024, when scores of down ticket nobodies were elected on his coat tails.

Plenty of candidates who steered well clear of the jamboree clearly disagree.



Obviously still loved in the convention hall, tanking approval ratings and a fading star quality are getting to our ratings-obsessed chum as he demanded a sworn pledge of loyalty from the crowd.

But they had just gone absolutely wild . . . for another man.

Vice President JD Vance, just 42, put in the performance of his admittedly short career.

His pacey primetime speech hit all the right buttons for the politicos and dispelled some — well deserved — pundit views that he is just, well, a bit weird.



Having shed a few pounds and grown a few greys over the past year, Vance was relaxed, funny and fired up.

Dealing with a heckler so effortlessly some suggested it must have been a scripted plant, JD — as the room chanted — stepped up to the plate and, frankly, knocked it out the park as they say here.

Having endlessly let it be known he was against the war in Iran all along,

Vance’s speech went hard on disgruntled MAGA fans, mis-sold an America First isolationist dream, urging them not to “throw the baby out with the bathwater”.



Trump’s mealy mouthed midterm campaign riff, that the Republicans are mainstream compared to the now extremist woke left Democrats, was distilled far more clearly by Vance: “It’s common sense or the crazies.”

Though he chickened out of mentioning Iran by name, “don’t hand over the country to a bunch of crazy people just because you disagree with a policy decision”, landed exactly where JD aimed it.

While he got a thumbs-up from Trump at the end of the speech, the speed at which the No2 was rushed from the stage, not even to return for the sing-along and balloon-laden end-of-convention ceremonies, said it all.

I would not have wanted to be any other leading Republican eyeing a tilt at 2028, judging by the roar of that crowd.



For the first time there’s a real buzz around JD, which might explain why increasingly respected Secretary of State Marco Rubio has briefed that he has “no plans” to run against his close buddy.

While Texas Senator Ted Cruz is clearly eyeing another doomed bid, other floated candidates such as the berk-ish Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth and loony tunes ex-intelligence chief Tulsi Gabbard need to give their heads a wobble before getting into the race.

The consensus from behind the scenes in Texas is only the man Trump once derided as Lil’ Marco could upset the JD juggernaut.

At 55, Rubio is a spring chicken compared to recent Presidents but he still carries the scars from his 2016 bid.



It would be highly unusual for a sitting VP to seek the nomination for the top job and not get it, so there’s a pecking order to contend with and plenty of MAGA powerbrokers are already locked in for Vance.

While establishment Republicans and plenty of big donors are urging the smoother and more traditionally conservative Rubio to change his mind, some wise hands say he would have a stronger bid in 2032 should Vance shoot and miss in two years’ time. Which could well happen.

Barely a Senator before he was thrust into the White House, it’s going to take more than one decent speech and a powerful back story to prove Vance is ready for the big seat.

A few years ago he was calling Trump “Hitler”, now he acts like his boss is the second coming. One minute he’s the true isolationist, the next he is meddling in European politics.

Hyper-online, White House insiders are quick to warn of his occasional hotheadness.



Truth be told, the Republicans may have the making of a winner here but they don’t know for sure. Which is why anointing him Trump’s successor without a proper contest may spell disaster.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The big guy’s endorsement will certainly end the primary hopes of any other candidate but even Trump seems hesitant, publicly stating he is not sure who would be the best candidate between his VP and top diplomat.

Despite the cheers of the crowd, Trump was far from alone as the Republicans headed off from Texas for the stump . . .

News.title: National security must ALWAYS trump welfare because without it, the entire country is reduced to a heap of cinders
News.content:
Benefits state

BRITAIN’S Armed Forces are running out of ammo and manpower — but there’s cash coming out of our ears for the workshy.

Andy Burnham admitted as much when he told MPs he would not cut the bloated benefits bill to boost military spending. He insisted he would never be forced to choose between the two.



But it’s clear he already has — and that welfare is the hands-down winner.

At a time when our defence capabilities urgently need bolstering amid the mounting threat posed by Russia, Iran and others, we face the jaw-dropping reality that the number of people who claim state handouts for ADHD has almost doubled in the past three years to 100,000 — while the number of full-time soldiers has shrunk to just 82,000.



In addition, the 70,000 people claiming benefits for anxiety now outstrips the combined full-time personnel of the Royal Navy and the RAF.

Since Labour grabbed power, the total welfare bill has shot up by a staggering £20billion a year. It’s not so much Benefits Street as Benefits State.

Those who are unable to work because of genuine disability deserve support.

But it’s right to ask why these numbers are suddenly rocketing at a time when shameless “sickfluencers” are teaching millions how to game the system.

If the PM is as keen as we think on turning the clock back six decades, he should heed the words of a Labour big beast from that period.

Denis Healey, who served as Defence Secretary and Chancellor, warned that national security must ALWAYS trump welfare, education and housing.



Because without it, the entire country is reduced to a heap of cinders.

Ship has sailed

LABOUR’S much trumpeted “one in, one out” deal to return illegal migrants was exposed as a failing gimmick months ago.

About 1,400 have been swapped so far — that’s a drop in the Channel when 20,000 have made the crossing already this year, and 50 of those kicked out simply returned on the next boat.

Now France wants us to take asylum-seekers from across Europe in a replacement for the agreement, which expires next month. Ministers should accept this stunt is dead.

It’s time to sink it and launch a serious deterrent to stop asylum cheats coming here in the first place.



PM’s drill rap

IN his first words to the Commons as PM, Andy Burnham promised a “place first rather than party first” approach.

So why is he set to delay giving the go-ahead for gas drilling in the North Sea until after a crunch by-election next month?

Simple. He’s scared it will help Green Party leader Zack Polanski to storm to victory in Sir Keir Starmer’s old seat.

His bold new politics have been shelved so he can cynically drill for votes instead.

News.title: Migrant hotels will be EXEMPT from Burnham’s ‘tourist tax’ as Tories blast ‘special treatment’ for illegal immigrants
News.content:
MIGRANT hotels housing asylum seekers will be exempt from Labour’s tourist tax as they are classed as “temporary accommodation”.

The exemption has stoked fears that hotels may decide to ditch paying guests and instead house migrants for the Home Office at a cheaper price.



Andy Burnham announced plans to let England’s 14 regional mayors impose an uncapped levy on overnight stays, on Wednesday.

The move sparked fury as it was revealed local leaders would likely slap the overnight levy on hard-working families staying in hotels, B&Bs and holiday lets.



However, taxpayer funded asylum hotels will not be subject to the tax, the Department for Housing, Communities and Local Government said.

The Conservatives were quick to slam the decision as “outrageous” as officials said the tax will hit hard-working families most.



Sources in the hospitality industry added that this may encourage more hotels to offer themselves up for asylum seekers rather than holidaymakers.

Chris Philp, the shadow home secretary, said: “It is utterly outrageous that families saving up for a break and struggling hospitality businesses will be hit with another tax, while hotels being used to accommodate illegal immigrants are exempt.



“British taxpayers should not be treated as a cash machine as asylum hotels get special treatment.

“Labour must explain why they think ordinary families should pay this tax but the asylum system should not. The answer is not another stealth tax on British families.

“We need to deport all illegal immigrants which would allow us to end the farcical hotel use entirely.”

James Cleverly, the former shadow housing minister, now running to be London’s next mayor, told The Telegraph it was a “perverse policy”.

He added: “Tourists spend money in the local economy, help keep our towns and cities vibrant and boost our prosperity. We should be encouraging them to come, not taxing them for the privilege.”



This follows estimations that UK families might have to add hundreds of pounds onto the cost of their staycations.

Trade group UKHospitality estimated the tax would add £99 to a week trip to London and £198 to the cost of a family summer holiday.

Meanwhile, school trips could also be subject to the levy unless local leaders choose to exempt accommodation used for “educational purposes”.

Business travellers would also be caught by the charge.

The Sun has been campaigning to Stop The Holiday Tax, warning it risks pricing hard-working families out of precious staycations.



We have urged the Government to ditch the plans amid fears they could hammer seaside towns and encourage Brits to holiday abroad instead.

The Telegraph reported that hospitality bosses were stunned after being briefed that England would follow the Scottish model, where there is technically no upper limit on the levy.

Industry chiefs had reportedly expected safeguards on how much local leaders could charge.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The chief executive of one leading hospitality firm said: “There will be a jobs bloodbath at a time when they’re trying to get young people into work.”

More than 100,000 hospitality jobs have disappeared since Labour came to power.

News.title: Moment fleeing drug dealer leaps from back of lorry after cops find £2m of cocaine stuffed inside Lidl bags as 2 jailed
News.content:
THIS is the shocking moment cops find cocaine worth £2million stuffed inside Lidl bags, stashed in a lorry.

Dzmitry Danilah and Klodian Marku have now been jailed for importing the class A drug after they were caught in an HGV with 50kg of the illegal substance.



Officers were inspecting a Renault Kangoo van parked in a layby on the A20 in Kent having spotted a cash counter on the back set.

While the patrol was checking over the van, they noticed an HGV nearby start to pull away and decided to follow it and eventually brought it to a stop on the side of the road.



Bodycam footage shows one cop climbing into the trailer of the lorry and he can be seen rummaging through several blue Lidl shopping bags.

He says: “Class A mate,” as he looks inside.



The driver, Danilah, whom they think is the only person in the lorry, is then arrested.

A second man, Marku, though can be seen diving from the back of the lorry as he attempts to flee.



An officer though manages to grab him and place him under arrest.

Cops then found the keys to the Renault Kangoo in his pocket when he was detained and searched, Kent Police say.

Danilah, 36, of no fixed address from Belarus, and Albanian Marku, 25, from Vauxhall, London, were later charged with the importation of cocaine.

Danilah was sentenced to nine years in prison and Marku received eight years at Canterbury Crown Court on September 9.

Investigating officer Detective Constable Molly Harrington said: “This is an extremely large seizure and is a result that was based entirely on the keen eye and intuition of our local officers.



“Disrupting such a large number of drugs from entering the market will have a significant impact on those behind this organised crime.

“The removal of dangerous substances will also crucially help prevent harm in our communities.”

News.title: Man arrested after black woman found hanging from tree in Mississippi
News.content:
Man arrested after black woman found hanging from tree in Mississippi

The body of Tasia Fortune was discovered hanging in the backyard of an abandoned home in Jackson, Mississippi on August 3 - the death has since been ruled as a homicide

View 2 Images Pictured: Tasia Fortune (Image: GoFundMe)

A man has been arrested in connection with the death of Tasia Fortune, a black woman who was found hanging from a tree in Mississippi.

‌



Police discovered Fortune’s body hanging in the backyard of an abandoned home in Jackson on August 3. The state medical examiner’s office determined that the death was a homicide, Jackson Police Chief RaShall Brackney said.

‌



Brackney said at a news conference on Friday, September 11 that police had secured search and arrest warrants for the man and arrested him when they encountered him walking on the street.

‌



The medical examiner's determination allowed police to execute the warrants they already had on hand.

“This case remains active and additional arrests will be pending,” Brackney said.

‌



View 2 Images A Gofundme was started after the death of Tasia Fortune (Image: GoFundMe)

Christy Spivey, Fortune’s mother, said Friday after police told her of the arrest that, “I just started crying and told them ‘thank you, thank you, thank you.’”

Spivey said police did not share a motive or whether DNA led them to the arrest. Spivey said she did not know the man who had been arrested, but was asking her daughter’s friends if they knew him. Spivey described the family as “in disbelief” and “shock.”

Article continues below

“We still don’t have a lot of answers,” Spivey said.

Police discovered Fortune’s body hanging in the backyard of an abandoned home in Jackson on Aug. 3.

Fortune died less than a year after the hanging deaths of 21-year-old Trey Reed, a Black student at Delta State University in Cleveland, and Cory Zukatis, an unhoused white man in his 30s, in Vicksburg.

News.title: Mum-of-two's body found in park as her sister issues heartbreaking message to killer
News.content:
Mum-of-two's body found in park as her sister issues heartbreaking message to killer

Mum-of-two Natasha Connors Kernan, 29, was found dead in Ravensdale Park in Dublin on August 25, with Gardaí investigating her death as a murder

View 3 Images Natasha Connors Kernan (left) and her sister Kym Kernan

The sister of a 29-year-old woman whose body was found in a park has called on the person responsible to "own up to what you did" in a heartbreaking plea.

Mum-of-two Natasha Connors Kernan was found dead in Ravensdale Park, Dublin, on August 25, and police are now treating her death as murder.

Speaking to the Irish Mirror on Friday, Natasha's sister Kym Kernan, 28, appealed directly to the person responsible, saying: "Own up to what you did. You took a daughter, mother, you took a sister, you took a loved one. We need to know what happened to her and if anyone saw anything just please say it.

"Don’t keep it in because it’s not like we can get her back. We need to know what happened to her because we need to grieve in the way we need to."

View 3 Images The body of Natasha Connors Kernan was found in Ravensdale Park in Kimmage, Dublin, on August 25 (Image: Collins Photo Agency)

Kym described her sister as a devoted mother with a "bubbly" personality. "We are all destroyed over what happened. She was my best friend, I grew up with her my whole life," she said. "My sister was bubbly. No matter what room she went in she would light it up."

Natasha was a mother to two young children, a girl and a boy, who have been left devastated by her death, Kym said. "My niece is destroyed. She was a mammy's girl and she's destroyed," she said.

"I found the only way I could explain it was to say to her that she was in the park and she fell and hit her head. I didn't know what way to tell the story. It's not an easy thing to do."

View 3 Images Natasha Kernan Connors was 'so loveable'

Kym said she received a phone call from her father's girlfriend telling her that her sister had died. "It didn’t feel real and it still doesn’t. I don’t think it’s going to feel real until I find out who did this to her and why," she said.

The grieving sister said the fact Natasha was found in a park near Crumlin "made no sense", pointing out that her sister had been staying at her father's girlfriend's home and "was not homeless".

Kym added that she could not think of anyone who would want to harm her sister. "Everyone loved my sister. She was so loveable," she said.

Following Natasha's death, a video was circulated on social media in which Natasha's mother, Yvonne, stood between individuals who falsely claimed that her daughter's death was caused by a migrant.

Yvonne has since blasted the video as false, and Natasha's sister has now revealed that the family were told from day one that an Irish man was responsible for her death.

Kym said: "With my mam's situation, my mam is vulnerable enough without all this and she was pushed into that. We were told way before that it wasn't a migrant.

"We were told from the get-go that it was nothing to do with migrants. I was disgusted. Two of my brothers are Muslim and I'm sick of the fact that migrants are blamed for everything."

News.title: Budding journalists celebrated at prestigious awards as Mirror legend Hugh Cudlipp's legacy honoured
News.content:
Budding journalists celebrated at prestigious awards as Mirror legend Hugh Cudlipp's legacy honoured

Dozens of entries were received for this year's Hugh Cudlipp Student Award, but there were some worthy winners at the Mirror-sponsored annual awards in London, as Vernon Kay showed his support

View 4 Images Zaina Odubeko Jada Sara Naidu, Emma Monaghan and Tilly Harris were recognised on Thursday (Image: Philip Coburn/Daily Mirror)

Aspiring student journalists have been honoured for their extraordinary work at this year’s Hugh Cudlipp Student Award.

‌



The annual event celebrates young journalism and remembers the impact of our legendary Editorial Director on the entire news industry. Hosted by the London Press Club and sponsored by the Daily Mirror, the award gives a vital platform and prize to students who made an outstanding contribution for an article or video exploring an issue of public interest, fitting for the proud Cudlipp tradition.

‌



Dozens of entries were received and the quality of work was praised before the winner was announced. Emma Conaghan claimed the honour, after a n insightful and professional film on the vital issue of male eating disorders and exercise addiction.

‌



View 4 Images Winner Emma Conaghan spoke of her passion for the industry (Image: Philip Coburn/Daily Mirror)

Iran and US in nailbiting race against time over new Middle East shipping threat READ MORE :

Her documentary uncovered a blind spot in British healthcare, made more difficult to cover because of shame, stereotyping, and domineering gym-bro culture, with a great spectrum of interviewees, leading to original, engaging and emotional interviews.

The Mirror’s Editor-in-Chief, Chloe Hubbard presented the award, and said: “It was a pleasure to meet all the deserving winners of the Cudlipp Awards who are all at the beginning of their adventure into journalism.

‌



"The standard of the entries speaks to how competitive the industry is for young journalists now, with so many traditional routes becoming closed-off.

View 4 Images The Mirror's Editor-in-Chief Chloe Hubbard was on hand to honour winner (Image: Philip Coburn/Daily Mirror)

"It is harder than ever to get a foot on the ladder and I sincerely hope this recognition of their talents piques the interest of a wily news editor somewhere.”

‌



Emma wasn't the only young reporter recognised. Tilly Harris was h ighly commended, with her entry focusing on an under-covered area of the social media debate, laying bare the reality facing children on TikTok with an engaging and accessible investigation, translates into a punchy news story and a great talking point.

View 4 Images Vernon Kay spoke of the importance of the media in 2026 (Image: Philip Coburn/Daily Mirror)

Rashmi Varma was c ommended after a creative piece gets to the heart of a community, drawing the link between Southall's soaring diabetes rates and the prevalence of sweet shops and dessert bars on the high street.

‌



Jada Sara Naidu was also honoured after producing a powerful and beautifully shot documentary looking at modern Black Britain asking questions about the Windrush generation and where they feel at home.

The event, which included a keynote speech by The Sun's Victoria Newton, also included a talk from Vernon Kay, highlighting the importance of journalism.

An insightful and professional film on the lesser-covered issue of male eating disorders and exercise addiction. This entry had a great spectrum of interviewees, leading to original, engaging and emotional interviews. This documentary uncovers a blind spot in British healthcare, made more difficult to cover because of shame, stereotyping, and domineering gym-bro culture.

News.title: 9/11 anniversary: Trump makes speech at Pentagon after skipping Ground zero memorial service
News.content:
Almost 3,000 people were killed 25 years ago today, with millions around the globe still bearing the burden of September 11, 2001, to this day

Donald Trump has delivered a speech at the Pentagon in Virginia to mark the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 terror attacks.

The US president said "we will never, ever forget" the day America "came face-to-face with true evil," adding "that's why we fight today". He also vowed Iran will never have a nuclear weapon as he thanked those who continue to serve "in the war on terror".

Earlier this morning, a memorial service was held at Ground zero in Manhattan to mark the anniversary. Trump is reported to have skipped the memorial in New York as he was unable to make a speech.

Today marks 25 years since the morning of September 11 2001 when al Qaida terrorists hijacked four commercial passenger planes in the United States. At 8.46am American Airlines Flight 11 crashed into the North Tower of the World Trade Center, less than 20 minutes later, at 9.03am, Flight 175 tore through the South Tower Two, causing both towers to collapse.

A third plane was crashed into the Pentagon, in Arlington, Virginia, just outside Washington, DC. The fourth plane, Flight 93, crashed in rural Pennsylvania after the crew and passengers overpowered the terrorists on board, preventing it from hitting another target, thought to be the Capitol building.

The attacks killed 2,977 people from 90 nations – 2,753 people were killed in New York, 184 people were killed at the Pentagon and 40 people were killed on Flight 93. Many more have died from, or are suffering with, health conditions linked to the toxic dust which spilled into the streets of Lower Manhattan.

News.title: Assisted dying debate live: MPs reject bill after tense Commons debate as Esther Rantzen laments ‘tragic day’
News.content:
'My wife died in pain and anxiety'

Sat alone on Parliament Square, nervously waiting for the vote, is widower James Marment.

He is clutching a handwritten cardboard sign, which says: ‘My wife died in pain and anxiety in July. She should have had the right to decide how she died.”

His voice cracks with emotion as he tells The Mirror the way his wife Suzie, which he described as her ‘worst nightmare’ - she had been ‘locked in’ her body unable to move, speak or even blink.

He explained how Susie, a radiographer for the NHS for 40 years, from Battersea died of a very rare neurological disease called PML, a virus in the brain which causes ‘every faculty’ to fail.

“Her worst nightmare was to be locked in, being unable to hear and see what was happening and not being able to express herself and that’s what happened to her,” he said.

“She was given tremendous support and care at the Royal Trinity Hospice on Clapham Common but there is nothing they can do with a patient who is losing control over every faculty.

“She was such a caring person, who fundraised for McMillan, and she did not want her family to see her suffer in a way that caused them pain and anxiety. She was always thinking of other people. She was unable to move, to speak or even blink her eyes. We did not wish her to die like that.

“It was very distressing indeed, which is why I am here today. To try and help other people not to have to go through that.

“We knew she wanted to go months before but there was no way she could.

“I was beside her bed with her daughter when she finally died and it was a blessed relief for her and for us.

“She was a magnificent woman, one of life’s lovely people. She should not have had to suffer in that way.”

News.title: 'Donald Trump faces humiliation in a state that's been Republican for 30 years'
News.content:
Each week from now until November's Midterm elections, we're going to look at one of the states to watch. And few states are going to be as unexpectedly fruity as Texas.

"Texas?" I hear you say. "The Lone Star State? The home of JR, oil barons and steaks you could take a nap on? Surely there's no way such a deeply red state could be at risk of turning blue." That's what everyone thought, until a few months ago.

See, four-term Republican Senator John Cornyn - an establishment Republican - faced a primary challenge from the Texas attorney general, Ken Paxton. Cornyn had touted his long record of supporting Trump's agenda in the primary campaign.

But the President has a long memory and recalled Cornyn had had some misgivings about his candidacy back in 2016 and his return for a second go in 2024. So at the last minute, Trump endorsed Paxton, a more straightforward MAGA type, a few days before the election.

‌



And Paxton gave him a thumping in the Primary run-off, despite having quite the history of his own. There was the failure to disclose his investments, the accusations of securities fraud and the 2023 impeachment trial after he brought a lawsuit against Georgia, Pennsylvania, Michigan, and Wisconsin in 2020 over discredited election fraud claims.

But perhaps the most egregious of his misdemeanours was when he was caught on camera nicking a $1,000 Montblanc Pen that had been mistakenly left behind by another lawyer at the security checkpoint of a courthouse. The theft was captured on CCTV, which Democrat rival James Talarico used in an absolutely delightful campaign ad last month.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

Talarico is a former teacher and current member of the Texas House. While serving in the Texas House, he's been studying for a Masters in Divinity from Austin Presbyterian Theological Seminary. And in a state where Trump won by 14 points in 2024, Democrat Talarico is currently polling 5-11 points ahead of Paxton.

‌



So while Trump's influence on primary elections is undeniable, the Texas Senate race is going to be a real test of whether that influence carries over into a general election - even in one of the most traditionally red states in the country.

And if Texas flips...it's going to the story of election night.
