News.title: Mainoo looks primed for battle with Man City’s new-look midfield
News.content:
This was Manchester United’s first foray back into the Champions League for 1,003 days, but even with hazy memories of the competition, they know full well they are unlikely to have it this easy again in Europe this season.

After an unconvincing beginning to their Premier League campaign and with Manchester City the visitors to Old Trafford on Sunday, Michael Carrick will have been grateful for a gentle start to life back among Europe’s elite.

Little-known Sabah of Azerbaijan have quite the story to tell, but the closest they got to making this an awkward evening for United came in the first half when, already trailing 1-0, Joy-Lance Mickels miscued an inviting header from close range. Otherwise, it was one-way traffic.

United’s biggest threat on the night was complacency, but there was none of that. This was a professional, unfussy display with a few nice flourishes. Kobbie Mainoo impressed again in central midfield and Carrick was able to substitute a number of his best players early with the derby in mind, as well as resting Luke Shaw entirely.

Goals from Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes and Benjamin Sesko in the first half killed the game as a contest before Lisandro Martínez scored a fourth with just over 20 minutes remaining.

News.title: ‘All I see are dead bodies’: The survivors of Syria’s chemical massacres
News.content:
“Unfortunately, I am still alive,” says Mohammed Suliaiman Abo Alkair, his green eyes heavy and distant.

The 38-year-old steps from his living room onto the roof and gestures towards a cluster of trees – a lone patch of green in a sea of grey rubble. It was there, at two in the morning 13 years ago that the whistle of a rocket ended not in an explosion but a thud.

For a moment, there was relief; the feeling of being spared. But then came a cloud of the nerve agent sarin.

Almost everyone around Mohammed died. His family and one small boy in a neighbouring house were the only ones to survive.

That August night, as Damascus slept, forces loyal to the Syrian President Bashar al-Assad launched eight sarin-filled rockets at the opposition-held districts of Zamalka, Ein Tarma and Jobar. The US government estimated that 1,429 people were killed, including 426 children. Other estimates put the number at 1729.

For more than a decade, nobody was held to account. Mr Assad denied the attack, shielded those responsible and later used sarin again – at Khan Sheikhoun in 2017, and in at least ten further attacks documented by the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons.

Only after Mr Assad fled Syria in December 2024 did the prospect of justice emerge. Investigators for Syria’s new government have since uncovered previously undeclared chemical-munitions caches, and the authorities have detained 18 suspects. None has yet been tried or punished.

But as attention turns at last to justice, the survivors remain invisible, absent from the reckoning. For now at least they remain largely invisible.

News.title: What an AI Armageddon might actually look like
News.content:
Jacob Coxon has left AI developer Anthropic with a public reckoning. For three years, the 27-year-old Brit trained models at OpenAI and Anthropic.

Both AI startups acted irresponsibly, Coxon wrote on X on Wednesday. “The people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade,” Jacob Coxon warned.

The response from his manager arrived just hours later. Evan Hubinger, Head of Alignment Research at Anthropic, also confirmed the warning: “We are, in fact, earnestly convinced that AI could kill all humans! I think the probability of that happening within the next decade is greater than ten percent.”

Anthropic, he added, does not yet have a solution to this problem.

When the head of safety at a multibillion-dollar technology company casually predicts humanity’s downfall at the hands of his own product, the debate leaves the realm of academic thought experiments.

The warning comes from the engineers writing the code. Both developers point to an industry dynamic in which competitive pressures outweigh safety concerns.

But what exactly are AI developers afraid of? What is the hypothetical scenario in which artificial intelligence brings about Armageddon?

News.title: Stephen Fleming learning nothing from rout of Pakistan
News.content:
Stephen Fleming arrives next week to start his job as England Test coach and his first task will be to apply his famously meticulous mind to assess a whitewash of Pakistan.

England are not quite there yet. Rain denied them a two-day win at Edgbaston, Pakistan finishing 52 for two, another 268 behind after England’s 453 all out.

But when the game does finish, and England complete a rout that started with Ollie Robinson taking a wicket with the first ball of the series, it will be time to look ahead to a proper challenge: a three-match series against Test champions South Africa over Christmas.

That series will give Fleming a much better guide to where his team stand in the lead-up to the Ashes summer. This one is less clearcut. Fleming has been in daily contact with Joe Root and will lean heavily on him and Marcus North. the national selector, for insight, but drawing definitive conclusions is impossible because of the lack of competitive cricket.

A quartet of quicks has emerged, led by Robinson, whose 21 wickets in the series at 6.6 look like a misprint. A double-wicket maiden to start Pakistan’s second innings would normally be headline-grabbing stuff. This time it felt almost predictable, even disappointing for those wanting to see some sort of contest.

Sports.title: West Ham thrash Wrexham to go top of the Championship
Sports.content:
West Ham made easy work of Wrexham in a 6-0 victory at the London Stadium to make it four in a row and go top of the Championship.

With the look of a side still belonging to the Premier League, Nuno Espirito Santo's West Ham controlled the game from the outset, overwhelming the visitors at times.

Captain Jarrod Bowen opened the floodgates in the 28th minute, arriving at the far post to convert Manor Solomon's cross after a flowing move.

West Ham continued to press and doubled their advantage seven minutes before half-time. Taty Castellanos drove into the box before finding Joel Piroe, who made no mistake with a first-time finish.

There was no let-up after the interval and Konstantinos Mavropanos headed Bowen's inviting corner beyond Anthony Patterson just three minutes into the second half.

Castellanos added one of his own in the 63rd minute, finishing calmly after Kyle Walker-Peters drove forward before teeing up the Argentina international.

Mohamadou Kante made it 5-0 in the 76th minute, racing onto Manor Solomon's clever ball over the top before finishing past Patterson.

Solomon then got his reward for an excellent individual display, adding the sixth. Walker-Peters teed up the Hammers No 10, who controlled, turned and fired home despite Patterson getting a hand to the effort.

The result lifts West Ham to 14 points from six games, taking them above West Brom at the top of the Championship making a statement with 16 goals in their last four outings after a shaky start.

For Wrexham, it was a chastening night as their previously stubborn defence was breached six times to who suffered their heaviest league defeat in in over two decades.

All the goals from the London Stadium

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Joel Piroe doubled West Ham's lead

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Konstantinos Mavropanos headed in West Ham's third of the night

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Castellanos made it four for West Ham

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mohamadou Kante scored West Ham's fifth goal of the night

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Solomon's stunner rounded off West Ham's goals on the night

Analysis: West Ham make statement that should strike fear into the Championship

Sky Sports' William Bitibiri at the London Stadium:

"It's one thing to win four league games in a row, but to put six past a Wrexham side that had conceded just five goals in their opening six games shows the level this team are currently operating at.

"There was an 'FA Cup third round' kind of feeling to the game that should put the rest of the division on notice.

"West Ham were aggressive, played with intensity and, importantly, never took their foot off the gas.

"There was a ruthlessness to them that you want to see from a team serious about bouncing straight back to the Premier League.

"Bowen, Solomon, Piroe and Castellanos all contributed, while Mavropanos added another goal from a set-piece.

"What impressed me most was the mentality. At 3-0, 4-0, even 5-0, they kept pushing.

"They've gone top, made it four wins in a row and scored 16 goals across those victories. That is a statement of intent."

The managers

West Ham's Nuno Espirito Santo:

"It's a good game, and that's very important for us. For them, it's good to score, to have confidence, and we know that we have to go again, but we are in a better place.

"The last one was a big moment, a big, big moment. Everything can change. But after that, I think overall, in terms of chances, we were really good.

"We didn't allow too many chances. We pressed them well, we organised, so it was good.

"It's so important that not only this game, but the players that are coming from the bench bring this energy."

Wrexham's Phil Parkinson:

"For 25 minutes we were in the game and then two moments where our defending wasn't good enough. We gave a team already full of confidence a huge lift and the third goal kind of really killed us tonight.

"Part of me is being reasonable and saying that these are a very good side, they've got a multi-million pound attacking force, probably a strike force which could be in the Premier League, but equally we can do a lot better.

"We've always, whatever division we've been in, wherever we've played, had the ability to show resilience and stay in games and give ourselves a chance.

"Tonight, after those first two goals, we kind of lost our way and we've got to analyse that quickly as a group and put the fundamentals back in place to give ourselves a chance in the next game."

Sports.title: Wigan storm to Super League's League Leaders' Shield and remain on treble course
Sports.content:
Super League: Wigan Warriors storm to League Leaders' Shield success with win vs Catalans Dragons and remain on treble course

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Wigan Warriors clinched the second leg of a potential sensational treble by winning Super League's League Leaders' Shield on Friday Wigan Warriors clinched the second leg of a potential sensational treble by winning Super League's League Leaders' Shield on Friday

Wigan Warriors clinched Super League's top spot and the League Leaders' Shield after a final-round 50-12 victory over Catalans Dragons, meaning Matt Peet's side remain on course for a domestic treble.

Having clinched Challenge Cup glory in May at Wembley with victory over Hull KR, Wigan lifted their second piece of silverware on Friday via a dominant home win over the Dragons.

Warriors scored nine tries through Harry Smith, Liam Marshall (two), Brad O'Neill, the retiring Liam Farrell, Austin Daniel, Jai Field, Zach Eckersley and Adam Keighran. Keighran also added 14 points off the kicking tee.

The only other side capable of claiming top spot and the League Leaders' Shield had been Leeds Rhinos, and owing to their far greater points difference, a victory over Hull FC would have been enough had Wigan slipped up, but Peet's side ensured that was never likely to happen. In any case, Leeds fell to a shock 18-12 home defeat to Hull on Friday.

Wigan will now seek to finish their season by clinching a treble with Super League Grand Final success at Old Trafford on October 3, having suffered final defeat last season to Hull KR. They and Leeds will have next week off as the play-offs begin, before contesting respective semi-finals at home on September 25 and 26.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Wigan Warriors win their sixth League Leaders' Shield and lift the trophy once again Wigan Warriors win their sixth League Leaders' Shield and lift the trophy once again

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Liam Farrell scored a try for Wigan Warriors having announced his impending retirement Liam Farrell scored a try for Wigan Warriors having announced his impending retirement

Keighran: We're going into the Play-Offs with plenty of momentum

Wigan Warriors' player of the match Adam Keighran told Sky Sports:

"It was good to finish like that. The scoreboard is nice but it's the way we went about it.

"We spoke about going into the Play-Offs with a bit of momentum and that was the perfect way to do it.

"We've still got things to fix up and that's what we'll talk about next week, but it's good to have that and still win games like we did today.

Adam Keighran and Liam Farrell scored tries in rampant Wigan's victory

"It was a group decision [Liam Farrell's late conversion attempt]. Someone said it in the huddle. With the career that he has had, you want to give blokes like him opportunities to do that.

"It's such a credit to Faz, he's unbelievable, the leadership that he's got, he's such a genuine bloke and I'm glad we can get a result like this and he can go out and lift the shield."

Farrell: Winning League Leaders' Shield doesn't get recognition it deserves

Wigan Warriors' Liam Farrell to Sky Sports:

"It [League Leaders' Shield] doesn't get the recognition it deserves. We spoke about it early in pre-season as something you want to knock off.

"You are slowly chipping away at it throughout the year. We've got there and this is a great end to the year and to do it like we did it tonight is great.

"I don't know the answer to that [is tonight final game?]. It's just all been about getting back to being fit. I've ticked that box. I had the conversation with Matty Peet, I said: 'Look, I'm there if you need me'.

"I didn't know how long I was going to play, I asked him before kick-off and he said 50 minutes, I was expecting about 10.

Farrell, Harry Smith and Jai Field were among the scorers as Wigan notched nine

"I wouldn't like to be picking a player of the year this season. There's been some great players and in championship teams you need a lot of good players and we've got a few of them.

"I was lucky enough to get over. Funny, I scored on my debut and then again on the final game of my career."

Peet: I never expected this coaching success

Wigan Warriors head coach Matt Peet told Sky Sports:

"I never expected to be at this stage of my coaching career with so much success. It's impossible to expect that.

"There was doubt, plenty of fear and day by day, week by week, I'm lucky enough to work with the people that I work with.

"My job is to try and keep it on the tracks."

Wigan head coach Matt Peet has now guided Wigan to nine trophies in five seasons

Asked whether this would be Farrell's last game, Peet said:

"No. In one way it was a good chance to celebrate it, I was always going to put him in this, because he deserves that. But now I've got to pick the 17 that gets the job done.

"He's a good player to have. I have a lot of gratitude to my players, still feel like... not an imposter, but it is a privilege to be associated with the club and play my part.

"This trophy represents the club more than the others, you know the consistency."

Arthur blasts 'erratic, poor' Leeds following home defeat to Hull

Leeds Rhinos head coach Brad Arthur told Sky Sports:

"We were a bit erratic at times. Some of our skill with the ball was very poor.

"We created more than enough opportunities. More than enough field position. Our forwards did more than enough on our edges and we were poor on our edges with our execution.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Hull FC beat Leeds Rhinos 18-12 at Headingley in the final round of the Super League regular season Hull FC beat Leeds Rhinos 18-12 at Headingley in the final round of the Super League regular season

"It's an individual thing. Our skill was poor. We created enough chances and had enough field position.

"We have two weeks, new competition. But we're not happy with our performances at home. Not good enough. This place needs to be a tough place to come and play."

Sports.title: Mumtaz: Razaullah wrote 'perfect chapter' to revive reeling Pakistan
Sports.content:
Former Pakistan captain Urooj Mumtaz lauded youngster Razaullah and said he wrote the "perfect chapter" to revive his reeling side after his sensational 81 off 63 balls against England on day three at Edgbaston.

Razaullah, who has only played eight previous first-class matches in his career, smacked nine sixes in his remarkable innings, equalling Tim Southee's record for the most maximums for a Test debutant, dazzling in a 121-run partnership with Mohammad Abbas (42) that eventually propelled Pakistan to a total of 449 and set England a target of 130.

The 21-year-old consolidated an already impressive performance on debut with the ball, taking four wickets in England's innings, including that of skipper Joe Root for his first.

His performance with the bat was undoubtedly the deciding factor in forcing the match into a fourth day that looked so improbable when he arrived at the crease, when Pakistan trailed by two runs at 318-8.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Razaullah smashed nine sixes to equal Tim Southee’s record for the most by a player on Test debut during a remarkable innings against England at Edgbaston.

"His innings was simply sensational," Mumtaz said on Sky Sports. "A perfectly written first chapter of his Test career. All that passion, the flair of Pakistan cricket!

"One 21-year-old who wasn't even on the list gets on the plane and gets his baggy green. Then Joe Root is his first Test wicket, he takes a four-fer on debut, and makes 81, with nine sixes.

"All of Edgbaston and all of Pakistan were on their feet!"

'Razaullah showed the beauty of Pakistan's raw talent'

Image: Razaullah equalled Tim Southee's record for most sixes on Test debut with nine

Mumtaz praised the spirit that Razaullah embodied, especially in the face of an off-field crisis that saw seven changes to the tourists' squad and a head coach axed ahead of the third Test after two heavy losses to begin the series.

"He showed the beauty of Pakistan and their raw talent - even he doesn't know what he's capable of!

"He's come off the plane and has absolutely no baggage. Yes he has a first-class hundred in dramatic fashion, but his hand speed is so quick he is ripping through the ball.

"He sits so deep in the crease and barely any of his boundaries are mishits - all of his sixes were monsters.

"That's the spark, the energy, the exuberance of youth that you are looking for.

"There was a smile on his face and he was not overwhelmed by the occasion. He didn't look in awe of it - he almost looked like he believed."

Razaullah: I just had to bat - you got to enjoy it!

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Nasser Hussain labelled Pakistan’s selection of Saim Ayub as a ‘disrespect for Test Match cricket’ after they flew out the batsman for his first class game in 11 months, just 10 days after playing in the CPL.

Pakistan debutant Razaullah, using Urooj Mumtaz' translations after speaking to Sky Sports in Urdu:

"I just had to bat, you are the ones who get to enjoy it!

"I was planning to take it longer and deeper - 81 runs is not bad though!

"The ball was in my slot - I was eyeing that up and trying to provide support for the other batters and trying to take it as deep as possible - I broke both my bats and wore down my third.

"There was no point at which I didn't enjoy it or when I was scared.

"I was wanting the strike, and overall I wanted to keep the strike as long as possible to get Pakistan another day."

Do Pakistan have any chance?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Dan Lawrence produced a stunning catch at slip off Gus Atkinson to dismiss Shan Masood for 95, denying the Pakistan batter a century at Edgbaston.

Mumtaz praised the role of fellow tail-ender Abbas - who notched his highest-ever Test score - in the partnership, and refused to rule out a miraculous comeback for Pakistan:

"A perfect script.

"To put one youngster in to bat with one stalwart of the game in Mohammed Abbas who is now on the honours board at Lord's after an eight-year gap between fifers," Mumtaz added.

"Abbas said 'I'm not just a seam bowler - I'm going to hit a few down the ground,' and he did!

"It all just amalgamates to show what could have happened if Pakistan had the temperament, the flair and the technique to back it up for the twelve-odd days of cricket we've had.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The Sky Sports Cricket team analyse a remarkable third day at Edgbaston as Pakistan fought back from a huge first-innings deficit, with debutant Razaullah’s explosive 81 helping set England 130 to complete a 3-0 series sweep.

"If anyone is a betting person, after what's happened today, it's almost like that dimming light has been ignited again.

"You never know [what will happen]. Razaullah had a four-fer on debut [in England's first innings], and he provides a point of difference with pace.

"They'll have to believe - there will have to be words of wisdom - and also know that there's not too much to be said.

"They can leave it at that, watch some tapes and come back tomorrow with hope."

Sports.title: Will it be a Sabalenka 'three-peat' or maiden US Open for new No 1 Rybakina?
Sports.content:
Two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka is looking to become the first woman to achieve the 'three-peat' in New York since Serena Williams in 2014 but she faces incoming world No 1 Elena Rybakina in the US Open final on Saturday.

Rybakina's results this year, starting with her Australian Open final triumph against Sabalenka, will see her rise to the top of the rankings on Monday, ending the Belarussian's 99-week reign.

But Sabalenka can exact some revenge for both that defeat and being overtaken at the WTA summit by defending her US Open title against Rybakina in Saturday's Flushing Meadows final - live on Sky Sports Tennis from 5pm.

"I really understand about how tough it is to reach the world No 1," said Sabalenka.

Like, everyone chasing everyone, and it's all about little things that you improve and you get better at."

Sports.title: Remarkable Razaullah knock denies England series sweep inside three days
Sports.content:
England were denied a series sweep of Pakistan inside three days of the final Test at Edgbaston after a remarkable display of six-hitting from 21-year-old Razaullah late on Friday.

Pakistan enjoyed easily their finest day of what's otherwise been a dismal series but were still trailing by two when their eighth wicket fell early into the evening session, only for Razaullah to smash 81 off just 63 deliveries, clearing the ropes a staggering nine times to equal Tim Southee's record for a debutant.

He shared in a 121-run partnership with Mohammad Abbas (42), who himself hit two sixes before picking out point off Josh Tongue in the closing overs, while Razaullah's fun was finally ended - and the day's play - as he was stumped off Dan Lawrence (2-17).

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Razaullah smashed nine sixes to equal Tim Southee’s record for the most by a player on Test debut during a remarkable innings against England at Edgbaston

England, guilty of losing the plot in the final session, will now look to chase down 130 on day four, a far stiffer target than initially looked likely, albeit one they should still reel in to clinch a first ever home series whitewash of Pakistan.

Score summary - England vs Pakistan, third Test, Edgbaston Pakistan 133 all out in 33.5 overs in first innings (put in to bat): Saud Shakeel (43), Mohammad Abbas (21); Josh Tongue (4-42), Ollie Robinson (3-15), Jofra Archer (3-25) England 453 all out in 89 overs in first innings: Harry Brook (75), Jamie Smith (69), Dan Lawrence (65), Emilio Gay (60), Ollie Robinson (50); Razaullah (4-148) Pakistan 449 all out in 96.4 overs in second innings (lead by 129): Shan Masood (95), Razaullah (81 off 63 balls), Babar Azam (76), Azan Awais (59); Gus Atkinson (3-109)

The tourists might be cursing not testing England further, with Shan Masood (95) and Babar Azam (76) both spurning golden opportunities to score the first century of the series.

While Masood can count himself a touch unfortunate, out to a screamer of a catch by Lawrence - one-handed, diving low to his right in the slips - Babar's dismissal was much more of a head-scratcher, the captain walking straight into an obvious short-ball trap set by England on the stroke of tea.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Dan Lawrence produced a stunning catch at slip off Gus Atkinson to dismiss Shan Masood for 95, denying the Pakistan batter a century at Edgbaston

That wicket had seemed to signal the end of the Pakistan resistance, with four wickets falling for 40 runs before Razaullah very much had other plans and pushed things into a fourth day with some almighty swings of the bat.

Resuming the third morning on 52-2, the visitors had been watchful to start, with only 15 runs added from a rather sedate opening 7.2 overs, before they suddenly sparked into life and smashed 117 off the next 20 - the wicket of Azan Awais (59) to a feathered edge down leg off Lawrence the only blot on their morning's work.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Dan Lawrence claimed England’s first wicket of day three as Azan Awais fell for 59 following a successful Joe Root review and sharp catch from Jordan Cox

England's four-pronged pace attack hadn't experienced such a session of toil this series without reward, but were improved after the lunch interval, with Gus Atkinson's initial eight-over burst particularly impressive as he finally secured his second wicket of the series, Masood undone by Lawrence's brilliance in the slips.

Babar was Pakistan's next bright hope for a hundred, what would have been his first in Test cricket for almost four years, but England turned to Jofra Archer and Tongue for a bit of bouncer theory and Babar simply couldn't resist taking it on despite repeated warnings.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jordan Cox takes a superb catch to dismiss Babar Azam in Edgbaston

It was Tongue (2-106) who finally got his man, Babar gloving one behind, while Archer (1-120) accounted for Saud Shakeel (29) soon after the tea break with another brute of a short ball that he could only balloon to short-leg.

A couple of terrific catches from Jordan Cox behind the stumps then accounted for debutants Ghazi Ghori (16) and Mohammad Imran (4) as Atkinson (3-109) located their inside and outside edges, respectively.

But Pakistan's third debutant, Razaullah, having already impressed with the ball - claiming four first-innings wickets, including that of England's leading Test run-scorer Joe Root in his first over - put on yet another show with an extraordinary display of ball-striking to not only see his side into a lead, but a 129-run advantage at that.

Beyond even his boundary-clearing blitz, there was terrific drama late on when he had an lbw decision against Lawrence overturned on review, only for him to perish the very next ball and what would prove to be the last of the day.

Razaullah: I just had to bat and get Pakistan another day

Razaullah, speaking to Sky Sports Cricket after his 81 off 63 balls:

Image: Razaullah laughs with Mohammad Ali in the midst of his magnificent innings on the third evening at Edgbaston

"I just had to bat, you are the ones who got to enjoy it.

"I was planning to take it longer and deeper - 81 runs is not bad though.

"I was just trying to provide support for the other batters and trying to take it as deep as possible.

"There was no point at which I didn't enjoy it or when I was scared.

"I won't give any messages to the batters - they can do their bit - but I really, really enjoyed it.

"I was wanting the strike, and overall I wanted to keep the strike as long as possible to get Pakistan another day."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The Sky Sports Cricket team analyse a remarkable third day at Edgbaston as Pakistan fought back from a huge first-innings deficit, with debutant Razaullah’s explosive 81 helping set England 130 to complete a 3-0 series sweep

Urooj: Razaullah provided spark | 'Pakistan have to believe'

Sky Sports Cricket's Urooj Mumtaz:

"That was simply sensational. A perfectly written first chapter of his Test career. All that passion, the flair of Pakistan cricket.

"One 21-year-old who wasn't even on the [squad] list gets on the plane and gets his baggy green - Joe Root is his first Test wicket, a four-for on debut, and then 81 with nine sixes - all of Edgbaston and all of Pakistan were on their feet.

"He's come off the plane and has absolutely no baggage. That's the spark, the energy, the exuberance of youth that you are looking for.

"There was a smile on his face and he was not overwhelmed by the occasion. He didn't look in awe of it - he almost looked like he believed.

"If anyone is a betting person, after what's happened today, it's almost like that dimming light has been ignited again.

"You never know. Razaullah provides Pakistan a point of difference with pace, and they'll have to believe."

Sports.title: Ballon d’Or shortlist shows up Premier League’s attacking failings – but tide could be turning
Sports.content:
Premier League representation is low when it comes to the 16 attacking players on this year’s Ballon d’Or shortlist. Manchester United’s Bruno Fernandes and Manchester City’s Erling Haaland are there but Cole Palmer, one of the nominees in 2025, is out after an injury-hit year and English football’s shift towards physicality and set pieces last season is summed up by none of the forwards from the best team in the country making the cut.

The trio giving Arsenal a presence – Gabriel Maghalhães, Declan Rice and William Saliba – are all defensive minded. Arsenal won the league but their forwards are not regarded as elite. Injuries played a part, denying Martin Ødegaard, Kai Havertz and Bukayo Saka fluency, but Mikel Arteta’s side were not loved by neutrals. There was respect rather than admiration for their defensive rigour. There was an argument that a lack of ambition after going 1-0 up stopped Arsenal from beating Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League final.

It was a close-run thing, but a second consecutive European title for PSG was a victory for attacking football over the Premier League’s attrition. Luis Enrique’s side keep beating English opponents, and there was a similar vibe at the World Cup. Games flowed more in North America, in part because of officials clamping down on the “meat wall” at set pieces.

As for England, Thomas Tuchel’s plan to tap into the Premier League’s physicality failed. England retreated in their semi-final defeat by Argentina. It is also significant that not until Anthony Gordon’s goal against Argentina did an England attacker who played in the Premier League last season score at the World Cup.

“Spanish football demands a different level of tactical and technical intelligence,” Gordon has said since leaving Newcastle for Barcelona. “In England, sometimes intensity can cover up mistakes. You can miscontrol the ball and still recover by winning the next physical battle.”

The English top flight’s appeal partly rests on those bruising qualities but the grind went too far last season. How many classic games can you remember? Some of the top sides having disappointing campaigns did not help but across the board there was grumbling about an over-reliance on set pieces and goalkeepers being squashed during elaborate corner routines. Anthony Barry, Tuchel’s assistant, noted that the game had become congealed in the middle. There was an emphasis on long throws and timewasting. The league was harder to watch.

View image in fullscreen Anthony Gordon has said Spanish football demands a ‘different level of tactical and technical intelligence’. Photograph: Newhouse Media/MB Media/Getty Images

Now comes the shift. One of the themes during the first three weeks of the campaign has been the pace quickening. Lawmakers have reacted. The five-second countdown and threat of a restart reversal at goalkicks and throw-ins have forced teams to think twice about timewasting. The 10-second time limit on players leaving the pitch at substitutions has helped and a trial with tactical timeouts mean an outfield player will have to go off for at least a minute after the restart of play if their side’s goalkeeper has gone down injured.

Early days, of course, but the football has been enjoyable and the numbers are encouraging. There have been four matches in which both teams have had 14 shots this season, compared with only one at the same stage last year. According to Opta, the average ball-in-play time has increased from 55min 23sec during the 2025-26 campaign to 57min 14sec. Delay times are down from 29.2sec to 26.7sec. Excluding penalties, the percentage of goals from set pieces has dipped from 27.5% to 23.5%.

There are more fast breaks per game (2.27 compared with 1.94), more shots per game via fast breaks (1.9 compared with 1.75) and more goals from fast breaks per game (0.43 from 0.23). Chelsea, more transitional under Xabi Alonso, are flowing and have been involved in some wild games. Liverpool have replaced Arne Slot with the counterpressing Andoni Iraola. Newcastle have been rapid under Matthias Jaissle, who has played to the strengths of Harvey Barnes and Anthony Elanga. Roberto De Zerbi seems an outlier at Tottenham, who need to speed up. Manchester City may soon want more incision from Enzo Maresca. The Italian favours a methodical style but even Pep Guardiola was moving away from obsessive control last season. There is a sense that some managers are closer in style to Jürgen Klopp than Guardiola at the moment. Alonso’s style has seemed very similar to Klopp so far. His willingness to let talent breathe is also quite like Carlo Ancelotti; Palmer has spoken about being allowed more freedom to roam under Alonso.

Perhaps there will be a correction as teams wise up to each other, Europe kicks in and injuries bite. Perhaps it will amuse you to hear that Arsenal remain top for delaying at a corner (with an average of 43.2sec). Then again, last Sunday delivered the season’s first clash between potential title rivals – Arsenal taking on Chelsea at the Emirates Stadium – and the action was breathless. Chelsea did not hold back and it was interesting that Arsenal welcomed the end-to-end openness.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Havertz was full of imagination up front and Ødegaard, Arsenal’s creative hub, dominated. It is a fascinating development. Defence was Arsenal’s greatest asset last season; Rice was more influential than Ødegaard in midfield. Now the Norwegian looks rejuvenated. Fitness helps but so does greater freedom. Chelsea did not shut the game down, so Ødegaard ran it. The best player in the best team was not a defender. At those levels Ødegaard looks as good as Fernandes.

View image in fullscreen Florian Wirtz has struggled to adapt to the pace of the Premier League. Photograph: Allstar Picture Library Ltd/Richard Sellers/Apl/Sportsphoto

This matters. Florian Wirtz, a star in Alonso’s champion Bayer Leverkusen side, has come to England and found the pace difficult at Liverpool. The Premier League needs top talent to feel it can shine. The three Bayern Munich forwards on the Ballon d’Or shortlist – Harry Kane, Luis Díaz and Michael Olise – moved from English teams. PSG’s Ousmane Dembélé and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia are fresh for the business end of the Champions League in part because they aren’t being pushed to the limit by teams such as Brentford and Bournemouth on the weekend. Jude Bellingham, England’s jewel, has never played in the Premier League. Vinícius Júnior toyed with moving to Arsenal but stayed with Kylian Mbappé at Real Madrid.

The Premier League is the strongest and most competitive in Europe. Yet there has been a talent drain. It is easy to imagine the best forwards feel they will have more fun creating and scoring against less intense Bundesliga defences and have the freshness to compete for the Champions League, international tournaments and for individual prizes.

Look at how the four semi-finalists at the World Cup were well represented by Premier League defenders and defensive midfielders but not by wingers and strikers. Where are the stars? Those who have left have mostly not been replaced, which is why the Premier League could do with Bradley Barcola shining at Liverpool after his arrival from PSG.

Barcola succeeding could convince others to follow. If the France winger is worn down, though, it could have the opposite effect. The Premier League has to be careful. The new measures to tackle timewasting could be a gamechanger. There were only four added minutes at the end of each half when Arsenal beat Chelsea. It felt refreshing.

Sports.title: Kobbie Mainoo moves from outsider to main man after summer of hurt
Sports.content:
It was a sight the England press pack became increasingly used to seeing after the team’s World Cup matches over the summer. Kobbie Mainoo was invariably the first to leave the dressing room, walk through the mixed zone – eyes dead ahead, features impassive – and board the bus.

It was as if he could not get out of the stadiums quick enough and the further England progressed the more pronounced it started to feel. There was a real gap between Mainoo and the next England player to depart the stadium in the knockout rounds. The Manchester United midfielder is inscrutable, even in the heat of battle. It is part of his enviably unflappable temperament. It was no great leap to imagine what lay behind the mask – tremendous frustration as Thomas Tuchel kept on leaving him out.

Mainoo did not play a single minute at the tournament. He was an unused substitute all the way to the semi-final exit against Argentina, and when everyone expected to see him in the third-place playoff against France he did not make the bench. The Football Association said before the game he had picked up an unspecified injury.

For Mainoo it was a lost summer and yet it was physically and mentally draining all the same, what with the training and travel; the demand to stay focused as he waited and waited. Like every player who was part of a squad that reached the final weekend of the World Cup, he reported late for pre-season training with his club. Mainoo played the last half hour of United’s final friendly against Milan and that was it. On the opening weekend of the season, he was fit enough only to be a substitute at Hull, coming on with 23 minutes to go and United 2-0 down, en route to a damaging defeat.

There has been a spotlight on Mainoo, with some fans wondering how he would react to the suffocation of his World Cup dream; his treatment by Tuchel, who preferred Elliot Anderson and Declan Rice in the deeper midfield positions and, also, at various times, Reece James, Jude Bellingham, Jordan Henderson, Morgan Rogers and Nico O’Reilly. Nobody should have worried. Mainoo is made of stern stuff. United regeared their midfield to the tune of £155m during the transfer window, adding Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba. Baleba has not yet played because of injury, but as United prepare for Sunday’s derby at Old Trafford, it is Mainoo who has reasserted himself.

The 21-year-old has been outstanding in each of United’s matches since the opener at Hull – against Ipswich, Everton and then Sabah in the Champions League on Thursday night. The question for Michael Carrick in the derby will be Mainoo and who in front of the back four.

View image in fullscreen Kobbie Mainoo in action against Sabah in United’s 4-0 Champions League win. Photograph: Allstar Picture Library Ltd/Richard Sellers/Apl/Sportsphoto

There is a reason why the United support have adapted the lyrics to Billy Ocean’s Love Really Hurts Without You to declare that their team cannot play without Mainoo. A couple of statistics. In the past three games, he has attempted 211 passes and completed 201, which represents extraordinary security on the ball – particularly given the frequency with which he has it. Also, the degree of risk inherent to so much of what he does.

Then there is the number that shows he made a game‑high 15 defensive contributions against Ipswich and Everton. He is improving out of possession. As much as anything, though, it is the quickness of the feet, the hip-shaking feints and changes of direction; how he simultaneously keeps his opponents on their heels and recalibrates United’s angles of attack.

Mainoo, of course, has already made his big comeback this year. Ruben Amorim could not fit him into his 3-4-2-1 system; the Portuguese did not trust him defensively. But even so, it continues to feel absurd that Amorim did not give him a single start in the Premier League last season. Mainoo’s first in the competition came in January against City at Old Trafford after Carrick had taken over.

It was the first match of Carrick’s second spell as the club’s manager and nobody really knew how it would go. “The players … maybe myself [as well], the coaches, obviously you guys in the media,” Carrick says. Everything came together in spectacular fashion, United winning 2-0, Mainoo straight back into the groove that had helped him win over Amorim’s predecessor, Erik ten Hag.

If it was an ignition point for Carrick, it was the same for Mainoo, whose form for the remainder of the season helped to drive United to a third-place finish and convince Tuchel to take him to the World Cup. As an aside, Mainoo v Anderson, who completed a £116m move from Nottingham Forest to City in July, will be box office. Anderson was a target for United before City blew them away with their offer. He called City “the kings of Manchester” on the day he signed.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

United’s dominance of the derby in January was almost total and a key takeaway was the slick first-time football they played. Remember the passing sequence when Rayan Cherki was triangulated by Matheus Cunha, Luke Shaw and Bruno Fernandes? The click was immediate for Carrick. This is the type of stuff that he wants; what he needs to see more of against City as he hopes to locate a bit of early-season momentum.

View image in fullscreen Kobbie Mainoo had a delayed start to the league season because of his involvement with England at the World Cup. Photograph: Adam Vaughan/EPA

Carrick knows a deep-sitting tempo-setter when he sees one, the player of the pass before the pass, and he doubled down on this sort of technician with his summer reboot, especially in Tielemans. It was also noticeable that when the luckless Mason Mount, who is back from his latest injury, came on for Tielemans against Sabah, he did so in a deeper midfield role. Carrick’s idea is to play through the middle. It is about balls to feet, timing, distances.

“It was nice to get Mason on in the second half and Andrey Santos [for Mainoo] and keep seeing the same things,” Carrick says. “It’s the combinations and connections. Taking the ball and playing close together at times. We have the technical ability for the boys to take the ball in the middle of the pitch. A lot of it is on wavelength and understanding … where each of them want the ball, which we are developing. It’s probably something that we’ve done a bit more of this season.”

Carrick is expected to start Tielemans alongside Mainoo with Fernandes as the third midfielder. They will be up against Anderson, Enzo Fernández and Cherki. It is a mouthwatering showdown. It will be where the derby is won or lost.

Sports.title: West Ham cut loose to hit Wrexham for six and go top of Championship
Sports.content:
West Ham secured their fourth league win in a row as they returned to the top of the Championship with a thumping 6-0 win over Wrexham at the London Stadium. It was a marvellous display of attacking football from Nuno Espírito Santo’s side, who swept to victory with room to spare and six different scorers.

Jarrod Bowen got the ball rolling after 28 minutes, Joël Piroe made it two before the break, then Konstantinos Mavropanos, Taty Castellanos, Mohamadou Kanté and Manor Solomon all scored in the second half as the Welsh side were dealt a hiding. The performance was further evidence the Hammers are finding their feet in the second tier after failing to win any of their first three games following Premier League relegation.

They should have led inside seven minutes, Castellanos sending a free header from Solomon’s cross over from six yards. Bowen then got clear in the box from a quick throw, but his shot was turned against the crossbar by a reflex save from Anthony Patterson. From the corner that resulted, Mavropanos headed a foot wide at the far post.

Piroe was guilty of an awful miss midway through the half, leaning back and blasting high into the Wrexham fans behind Patterson’s goal. Bowen showed him how it was done a minute later. Morato’s cross from the right was timed perfectly into the six-yard box, where the home side’s captain was arriving ahead of Jacques Ekomié to guide it into the far corner.

Mavropanos cleared off the line from George Dobson with Mads Hermansen beaten, which proved to be the closest Wrexham would come to a goal. Castellanos stayed onside and strode on to a through pass before unselfishly squaring the ball for Piroe to make it 2-0 before the break.

Patterson prevented Solomon from putting the game beyond Wrexham in the first two minutes of the second half, racing from his goal to smother the forward’s low shot. It would be a momentary reprieve and under a minute later it was 3-0. From Bowen’s corner, Mavropanos was left free inside the six-yard box to head home.

Bowen flashed a shot inches wide after cutting inside as the besieged visitors teetered on the edge of an all-out collapse in east London. West Ham’s fourth came from a Wrexham corner. A poor ball into the box was collected by Kyle Walker-Peters, who dashed away on the counter, exchanging passes before teeing up Castellanos to slot the ball into the corner.

Kanté came off the bench and made it 5-0, a lovely rising finish after being sent clear by Solomon, then the Israel international completed the rout with a deflected shot via a post.

Sports.title: Premier League news: Iraola values Wirtz’s work ethic; Moyes backs ‘senior citizen’ Grealish
Sports.content:
1. Wirtz’s worth ‘not all about statistics’ Andoni Iraola has insisted Florian Wirtz should be judged by his influence on Liverpool rather than statistics and believes the player’s impact will increase as his rapport with a new-look attack develops. Wirtz impressed in Liverpool’s defeat of Atlético Madrid on Wednesday, having also produced some of his best performances last season in the Champions League. But he has also come in for criticism this season for the amount of times he has conceded possession. The £116m Germany international has one assist and no goals in the Premier League so far. “Flo played very well against Atlético Madrid and I also think he has been unlucky,” said Iraola. “I remember the ‘goal’ he scored against Nottingham Forest; they gave it live and then VAR disallowed it. He could have had very good assists but we haven’t finished them. That is why you cannot just play because of the numbers. “Whether a striker scores a lot of goals or he doesn’t, you have to look at the performances. Does he help us to play well? Yes. Well, someone will score the goals and someone will give the assists. I am not too focused on numbers. Nowadays everything is about numbers, everyone tells players you have to assist, you have to score goals. For me, you have to help us play well. Someone will score the goals and I don’t care if it is the midfielders like it was the other day. Someone will score the goals if we are doing well collectively.” Wirtz created an excellent chance for Bradley Barcola against Atlético and Iraola believes the 23-year-old will exert a greater influence as his understanding with the France international and fellow new signing Victor Muñoz improves. “There is an argument to make that the wingers have changed more than anywhere else,” Iraola said. “Now we have new weapons we can use with Bradley and Victor. With Florian, he is key for us. I am not worried because he will quickly learn where Victor prefers the ball or where Bradley prefers the ball. And, also, Bradley in just his second game you could see they already had a good association. I am not very worried.” Andy Hunter

2. Grealish ‘can be a wingers’ role model’ David Moyes has told Jack Grealish he wants him to become a role model at Everton for fellow wingers Tyrique George and Tyler Dibling. Grealish made an immediate impact from the bench against Manchester United last Sunday in his first outing since rejoining Everton on loan from Manchester City. Despite a lack of minutes in pre-season, as he recovered from the fractured foot that curtailed his first campaign with Everton, the 31-year-old could start for Moyes’s side at Tottenham on Saturday. The Everton manager wants Grealish to take on more responsibility this season. “Jack knows when he comes here there is an opportunity for him to play and to show what he can do,” Moyes said. “But I also want him to be a senior professional and a role model. We’ve got Tyrique and Tyler and if ever you are looking at somebody for how to play as a wide player, Jack Grealish would certainly be one of them. “I think both of them could learn an awful lot from Jack and I want him to become that senior citizen among them, somebody who teaches them. We’ve got a mature Jack Grealish now as well in terms of understanding the game and being a team player – not that he is an individual but he plays with an individual style.” Moyes believes there is greater expectation on Grealish given it is his second season at the club and there is a need to fill the creative gap created by Iliman Ndiaye’s departure. “If there is one person who would be able to carry that it would be Jack, just because of the way he is,” he added. View image in fullscreen Jack Grealish made an immediate impact from the bench against Manchester United last Sunday in his first outing since rejoining Everton on loan. Photograph: Adam Vaughan/EPA “He will find it easy to carry expectation and he’ll be happy to do so. That’s his character. Everybody wants Jack to get back to where he was. His first three months for us last season was hugely important in getting us wins so now it is about getting him right to perform at that level again. “He’s had six and a half months out. He’s had no pre-season games, he came on for 15 minutes in the Community Shield, so he’s had no real football and Jack is someone who thrives on the football. He gets himself fit through the games more so than the training. We need to be careful and see how he goes but he’s looking good.” Andy Hunter

3. João Pedro ‘as good as Haaland’, says Alonso Xabi Alonso has claimed João Pedro is at Erling Haaland’s level and similar in style to Karim Benzema. The Chelsea striker has reacted to missing out on Brazil’s World Cup squad by making an excellent start to the season and was named the Premier League’s player of the month on Friday. João Pedro has scored twice in his first three league appearances and has formed an exciting attacking trio with Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers. Chelsea have scored 16 goals in all competitions and Alonso did not hold back when asked if the 24-year-old is as good as Haaland. “I would say yes,” Chelsea’s manager said. “If you count how many top strikers we have in the Premier League, I’m sure that João is there. Haaland for sure is there. So I would rate him that way.” The range of João Pedro’s game has added to his threat. Alonso played with Benzema at Real Madrid and sees similarities between the pair. “In many things he reminds me of Benzema,” he said. “He is good in the box, he is good out of the box, he is good coming to his left side, he is good with the head, he is very complete, he is intelligent. Still young, still things to develop, but many, many absolutely outstanding qualities.” Chelsea host Hull on Saturday afternoon and will be looking for a strong home performances after fighting back from 2-0 down to beat Leeds 6-3 in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday. View image in fullscreen João Pedro has scored twice in his first three league appearances for Chelsea. Photograph: Paul Childs/Action Images/Reuters Palmer was key to the comeback and revealed that Alonso, who had rotated heavily, ripped into his players at half-time against Leeds. “I was angry with myself that I didn’t help the players to play better or have a better feeling,” Alonso said. “There is a moment that you try to explain what is not working well, try to make preparations and then there is a moment that you need to kick their arse a little bit, in a nice way. It worked – not for me but the players who came on with a better quality and better everything in the second half.” Chelsea will again be without Moisés Caicedo. The midfielder is yet to start this season and Alonso does not want to risk him. Jacob Steinberg

4. De Zerbi wants exile Richarlison to stay Roberto De Zerbi insists he does not regret the handling of Richarlison’s situation at Tottenham after the forward was omitted from his Premier League squad, even though Spurs are yet to score in the competition. De Zerbi said Richarlison had in effect exiled himself by refusing to sign a new contract and repeatedly saying he wanted to leave. The 29-year-old’s absence looks increasingly unfortunate for Spurs after three league matches. They have never gone four league games without scoring at the start of a season. De Zerbi described Richarlison’s omission as a “consequence” of the Brazilian’s actions over the past month and a half. A deadline-day move to Everton, who visit the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on Saturday, collapsed after Spurs had signed replacements. Richarlison continues to train with the first team. “If I had decided myself to leave him outside of the squad, I would have regrets,” De Zerbi said. “But the decision has not even been taken by the club.” The Italian said it would be “much better” if Richarlison were in his squad, happy to stay and “maybe to extend his contract, because he is still an important player, he was important last season, we can’t forget. But we can’t forget also the last 45 days.” De Zerbi is missing last season’s three top scorers: Richarlison, João Palhinha, who left for Benfica, and Cristian Romero, who joined Atlético Madrid. Mykhailo Mudryk signed on loan from Chelsea, picked up an injury in training. An ankle scan revealed ligament damage that will keep the winger out for about six weeks. De Zerbi feels the “silly injury”, caused by playing too much after being out for so long, could have been avoided. View image in fullscreen Roberto De Zerbi believes Sávio ‘can score more goals – even if he isn’t Harry Kane.’ Photograph: Andrew Boyers/Action Images/Reuters Sávio arrived from Manchester City for £75m, closely followed by Omar Marmoush on loan. Marmoush scored only 10 league goals in a season and a half at Manchester City, but was more prolific in the Bundesliga at Eintracht Frankfurt. “In terms of goals he’s not Harry Kane but he can score more goals than he has done in the last two seasons,” De Zerbi said. “If you analyse his qualities, he can score more goals and he has to demand more goals from himself. Even the stupid goals, he has to change his habits after being used to scoring the great goals.” De Zerbi says his players have lacked confidence and freedom on the pitch this season and challenged them to take more risks and show personality “like a big team” and “like big players”. Meanwhile, Lucas Bergvall has signed a new long-term contract. The 20-year-old wanted to leave in the summer but was convinced to stay by De Zerbi. Sam Cunningham

5. Manchester United take action against ticket touts Manchester United believe they have disrupted organised ticketing networks having removed 685 season tickets as part of a contentious ticket touting investigation. The club’s summer crackdown resulted in widespread condemnations from fans and supporter groups after many innocent people faced the threat of sanction. The 1958 this week called for fans to “stand united” against the “season ticket ban fiasco” in a protest before Sunday’s derby against Manchester City as a “line has been crossed”. United released an outcome update on their investigation before this weekend’s action, revealing that 685 accounts have been subject to a ban while 464 supporters received a reduced sanction or final warning. A club statement read: “Bans were issued where there was significant misuse of the ticketing system for financial gain. This included the operation of organised ticketing networks, which were controlling, selling and distributing tickets from hundreds of accounts. “These actions undermine fair access to tickets for genuine supporters and have no place at Manchester United. Our focus now turns to ensuring these tickets are returned to our supporters. All season tickets released through this process will be offered to supporters on the season ticket waiting list.” United say the investigation identified 1,617 accounts that required further review due to what it calls “unusual activity”. Of those stripped of season tickets, 113 failed to respond to requests for further information, 73 did not appeal and 499 received bans upheld by an independent appeals panel. Press Association

6. Jaissle hopes Fernandez-Pardo can face Leeds Matthias Jaissle revealed that summer signing Matias Fernandez-Pardo is edging closer to starting for Newcastle. The 21-year-old forward arrived on Tyneside from Lille on deadline day and has featured as a substitute in Newcastle’s last two matches. Speaking before Monday’s fixture with Leeds, Jaissle said: “Yeah, he’s getting closer. I said that we need to be smart with his load management. Now he’s getting more and more minutes. He has now almost a full training week to Leeds, that helps him a lot. I think it’s the first time now since he arrived, and then we can make the decision on Sunday, maybe even on Monday.” Jaissle was also pleased to see Tino Livramento continue his return from injury as the full-back got 45 minutes of football under his belt with an appearance from the bench during the second half of Tuesday’s Carabao Cup win over Millwall. “I’m happy for him that he got 45 minutes on a high level against a strong opponent in difficult circumstances playing there in Millwall,” the Newcastle manager said. “That makes us proud to see him already on a high level.” Press Association

Sports.title: Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall: ‘I’ve seen all of the meltdowns and it annoyed me’
Sports.content:
Transfer deadline day may be “exciting for everyone”, as Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall puts it, but his experience of that transfer deadline day at Everton hauled him through the same gamut of emotions as every Evertonian. Excitement turned to bewilderment before the conclusion of the window left the midfielder exasperated, but for entirely different reasons to a fanbase left questioning the club’s direction under The Friedkin Group.

How, now, is the mood in the squad? It is the obvious place to start after a deadline day that left David Moyes with fewer players than he had at the beginning, one striker and no cover for either full-back position. It also featured the US international striker Folarin Balogun walking out on a £40m transfer minutes after submitting a deal sheet. “Really good to be honest,” Dewsbury-Hall insists. “Definitely not the same mood as what I’ve seen on the outside. There’s a good mentality this year of: ‘We’ll show everyone.’” Everton’s performances so far this season support that view.

“I’ve seen all of the reactions, all of the meltdowns, and in all honestly it annoyed me a bit,” Dewsbury-Hall says in forthright and insightful fashion. “I get where people are coming from; everyone wants to sign everyone and have the perfect squad. But there are still 19 lads in this building who are going to hopefully take this club to good things this year. That was getting disregarded.

“I saw people saying: ‘We’ll be lucky to stay up this year.’ What message is that sending to the lads who are already here? I’m not blaming anyone. We get it. It didn’t work. But let’s all be positive – right, it’s done, bang, let’s go – and that’s what we’ve been trying to say in the dressing room. Of course we would have wanted to sign a couple more, but we’re happy with what we’ve got and it’s given us more impetus now to move on.”

Moyes has expressed concern over the signals Everton’s transfer business could send to the dressing room at a time when he is trying to push the team on. So has it had a detrimental impact? “Not really, no,” Dewsbury-Hall insists. “I know we’ve got a smaller squad but we’ve got some really good players. Our starting XI is top, a European starting XI.

View image in fullscreen Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall says he needed his move to Everton to avoid his career stagnating. Photograph: Tony McArdle/Everton FC/Getty Images

“I get it, you need a whole squad, but we’ve got 17, 18 players at a really, really good level. I don’t think a couple of years ago it was at that level. Actually I know it wasn’t. Things can be out of your hands in football and that’s what happened for us. But we quickly realised: ‘Hang on a minute, look around the dressing room – top player, top player, top player.’ If we’re doing the right things we can still be successful.”

Dewsbury-Hall will be crucial to those prospects. The midfielder has flourished since his £28m arrival from Chelsea last summer, his game-time and growing influence vindicating the decision to leave Stamford Bridge behind. “I’m in the prime years of my career,” he says. “I couldn’t afford to spend more years stagnating.” The 28-year-old’s influence extends behind the scenes. This summer, following Séamus Coleman’s departure, he was nominated for a new leadership group that was established to compensate for the loss of the long-serving Everton captain.

“Because Séamus has left such a big hole we need a group of experienced lads to crack on together and keep the standards high and to drive things,” Dewsbury-Hall explains. “It’s just the more experienced lads – [Jordan] Pickford, Tarky [James Tarkowski, the new club captain], Jimmy [James] Garner, myself. The ones that have been playing in the Premier League for years or feel like they are settled at the club.

View image in fullscreen Kiernan Dewsbury Hall lets fly in Everton’s impressive 2-2 draw with Manchester United. Photograph: Tony McArdle/Everton FC/Getty Images

“It’s nice [to be voted in after just one season] but it’s definitely an impact I wanted to have. I’m really pleased that the lads look at me as someone that can be important for the dressing room.”

That sense of responsibility is evident in Dewsbury-Hall’s mentoring of fellow midfielder Harrison Armstrong, the 19-year-old who almost joined Nottingham Forest before deadline day only for the furious response of Evertonians at Bournemouth to prompt a U-turn from the club’s owners. “They definitely made their feelings known and obviously it worked,” says Dewsbury-Hall. “Big credit to them for that, they were amazing that day. And I know for a fact it made Harrison feel very good and it helped him. He is a very confident lad and well respected in the dressing room for such a young age.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“If there is anything I can help him with then I will. Shooting’s definitely one because his shooting is sometimes not the best, and I’ve told him that many times. But he’s got pretty much everything else. He always likes to say he’s got a better strike than me so I just tell him to look at the [Crystal] Palace goal [that Dewsbury-Hall scored on the opening day] or the Wolves goal last season. We have good banter.”

The Nottingham-born midfielder is clear in his targets for this season: European qualification, which he contends can be achieved despite the smaller squad, a strong cup run, improvement in his all-round game and a first England call-up. His rising performance levels have not gone unnoticed by Thomas Tuchel, who names his squad next Friday.

Dewsbury-Hall says: “I know I’m the closest I have ever been now. You get a message two weeks before the squad is announced. I got one for the long list for the World Cup and I’ve had one for these next games. It’s nice. It means you are doing OK. It’s a long, long message. It tells you that it’s a legal requirement for us [the Football Association] to tell you in advance that you are in contention and to be available for these dates. It’s a good feeling because you think: ‘OK, I am close,’ but you know you have to keep pushing it to the last minute. It’s up to me. It’s got to be me that forces his hand to choose me. It’s not going to be given to me.”

Nor will anything be given to Everton, but Dewsbury-Hall and company will push on regardless.

Sports.title: ‘Delay the meals’: Mikel Arteta reveals latest maverick Arsenal methods
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta has revealed that he likes to set players challenges, such as delaying their meals before matches and making the dressing room hotter, to ensure they are fully prepared for any eventuality.

Arsenal’s flight to Italy on Tuesday for their Champions League opener against Napoli was delayed for more than five hours, with Arteta forced to cancel his pre-match press conference after the squad arrived in Naples just before 10pm local time.

The disruption proved no handicap as they made it 13 successive league-stage victories in Europe, thanks to Martin Ødegaard’s second-half winner.

Arteta has a reputation for his innovative methods having previously employed pickpockets during pre-season training camps and preparing for a trip to Anfield by pumping crowd noises through a speaker.

The Arsenal manager has now explained how his players have been trained to expect things to go wrong. “I love those challenges. I try to create them in pre-season,” he said. “So when they happen, we already experience them and we already know. So, get to the stadium very late, change the routine as soon as the players have to do something else.

“Because when it happens, and it can happen, you can miss the flight, the train can be delayed, there’s so much traffic, and I don’t want the players, the staff as well, panicking.

“So, when that happens, adapt to it. ‘OK, we have another two or three hours on the plane, how can we use them?’ Play together, spend some time together, sleep, use it, but ­certainly don’t complain and then use it as an excuse because that’s not helpful at all.”

Asked what other methods he has employed, Arteta added: “Just delay the meals, delay the transport, take a different route. We have done many things: make the dressing room hotter, more difficult, more challenging, less [massage] beds. Those kind of things. Because we are going to have to adapt to different contexts and we will try to anticipate it and create the best possible conditions. But when there is that element of stress or ­surprise on matchday, it’s important [to be prepared].”

Arsenal travel to Sunderland on Saturday night looking to extend their 100% start to the new campaign after being held to a 2-2 draw at the Stadium of Light last year. Leandro Trossard scored Arsenal’s second goal before Brian Brobbey’s late equaliser and Arteta contrasted the Belgium forward’s reaction to leaving in the summer with that of Gabriel Jesus, whohas complained that he was kept in the dark over his future before being sold to Barcelona. “No one told me nothing,” said the Brazilian, who was made to train separately from the rest of Arsenal’s squad before moving to Barcelona. Trossard, meanwhile, was at the Emirates for last week’s win over Chelsea having joined Beskitas in July.

“Very surprised, to be fair, especially because with Gabriel I had an individual talk in the dressing room,” said Arteta. “And the words that we used for each other, it was all about gratitude. So, I don’t know. It’s OK. Sometimes I understand when you have to deliver bad news or news that people don’t expect. Those things are reactive. Somebody has to be the bad cop; if I have to be, I have to be.

“What is important is normally what happens three months later, six months later. When Trossard comes in, he’s in the dressing room with all of us, the atmosphere and the relation you have with all the players that they left, at some point their relationship has been really good. I hope that’s the same case.”

Sports.title: Chelsea hand Pedro Neto new deal in wake of his rejecting Manchester City
Sports.content:
Chelsea have rewarded Pedro Neto’s strong start to the season and commitment to the club by handing the winger a new contract. The Portugal international had summer interest from several Premier League clubs including Manchester City, but indicated a desire to stay and play for Xabi Alonso. He has signed a five-year deal with the option of an extra year and is to receive a pay rise.

Alonso has used Neto as an attacking wingback and the 26-year-old has scored twice in five appearances. Neto, who has registered 40 goal involvements since joining from Wolves for £54m in 2024, follows other leading players at Chelsea in signing new deals. João Pedro, Reece James and Moisés Caicedo have received improved terms this year, and Cole Palmer signed a new deal in 2024 and committed his future to the club in an interview with the Guardian last season.

Chelsea’s owners have a strategy of giving lengthy incentivised contracts. However, the club have demonstrated that being on those multi-year deals will not stop players from receiving pay increases as reward for good performances. Further contract renewals are expected to be announced soon.

Neto’s determination to stay contrasted with the stance of Enzo Fernández, who was sold to City for £125m during the closing hours of the transfer window.

He was not handed a new contract after initial discussions were held. The Argentina midfielder raised questions over his future in March, criticising January’s departure of Enzo Maresca as head coach and sparking talk of a move to Real Madrid by expressing a desire to live in the Spanish capital. Chelsea responded by banning Fernández for two games.

Madrid downplayed their interest in Fernández but the 25-year-old continued to push for a new challenge. City, who appointed Maresca as Pep Guardiola’s replacement, emerged as Fernández’s strongest suitors. Chelsea were prepared to hold on to him if their valuation were not met but concluded that selling was the right long-term move. There was disappointment that one of the team’s senior players did not show better leadership when Chelsea were struggling. They missed out on European qualification after finishing 10th.

View image in fullscreen Enzo Maresca and Enzo Fernandez during their time at Chelsea. They have been reunited at Manchester City. Photograph: Mark Pain/Alamy Stock Photo/Alamy Live News.

Chelsea sacked Liam Rosenior in April and announced Alonso’s appointment in mid-May. They were willing to reintegrate Fernández but he is understood to have submitted a written transfer request. It is understood he also informed Chelsea he had been in contact with a former coach, believed to be Maresca, at the end of last season and during the transfer window.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The Stamford Bridge hierarchy concluded that Fernández’s relationship with his teammates was broken after his public comments. Fernández’s representatives have been approached for comment.

Sources have dismissed the idea that Chelsea were bullied into selling Fernández. Neto’s renewal is viewed as the latest evidence that key players have bought into the project and will be rewarded.

Sports.title: Olid’s United on back foot due to late business and unforgiving WSL start
Sports.content:
It was tough watching Manchester United’s players labour ineffectively against the hungry and aggressive press of London City Lionesses in the Women’s Super League’s opening match. Simi Awujo’s late consolation goal did little to ease the mounting concern for a side that have several teams nipping at their heels.

Don’t panic; that has to be United’s message. To an extent, it is very early to be writing the team’s obituary. The new head coach, Eva Olid, had only three weeks to try to implement her ideas about the way the team should play before that match in Bromley on Friday 4 September. That is not long enough for her to peel away Marc Skinner’s imprint on the team.

The forward Monica Jusu Bah did not arrive from the Swedish side Häcken until 28 August and Rebeca Bernal signed from Washington Spirit on 2 September. United’s late business, in regards to their managerial change and transfer activity, has put the team and coaching staff on the back foot, playing catch-up with clubs who got most of their business done early in the window, the better to capitalise on the opportunity for a full pre-season presented by the lack of a major international tournament.

The problem is the spotlight is harsh on the red side of Manchester. The minority owner Jim Ratcliffe’s dismissive comments relating to the women’s team and the lack of serious investment in the squad provide reasons to be somewhat forgiving of the head coach and her charges, their struggles an indictment of a club that seemingly do not fully care.

The focus is said to be on a sustainable investment model recruitment-wise and on developing younger players. In isolation they are admirable goals, but in the context of investment gathering pace at other WSL teams and the relative pocket change required at a club of United’s stature to have a transformatory effect on the women’s side, these goals become shackles.

There is some irony in Olid leaving Hearts and coming to United. She arrived in Scotland to take charge of an amateur team that had avoided relegation only owing to the expansion of the top division and within five years had taken them to professionalism and a Scottish Women’s Premier League title. She felt the level of investment then needed to make Hearts competitive in Europe was lacking and it was announced that she would depart at the end of the season. The WSL and its teams are miles ahead, developmentally, of the SWPL and its sides but Olid has landed at a club that have repeatedly failed to invest substantially enough to make them league or European title challengers.

Olid told the Catalan newspaper Ara that she would have stayed at Hearts “if my project continued”. She said: “I wanted to coach in Europe, but it was a preliminary round and perhaps we would be there for a week and get eliminated. I don’t want to go backwards, I preferred to leave after winning everything because otherwise I would feel frustrated.”

View image in fullscreen Manchester United only lost 2-1 at London City Lionesses last Friday but were outclassed throughout the game. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

Frustration was the name of the game at United under Skinner. The former head coach was frustrated with what he regarded as a lack of support in transfer windows and fans grew increasingly frustrated with a lack of sustained progress. United would take a step forward, such as winning the FA Cup in 2024 or reaching the Champions League quarter-finals last season, then fail to push on.

Patience is thin and Olid’s task has been made a lot harder by seven departures and only four additions to what many viewed as an already light squad. Olid has said she has had assurances that United will be active in the winter window. “We have some plans in January about signing players that I really need for my style of play and game model,” she said in her first press conference.

However, United have 12 WSL games before January, plus cup games, and with Chelsea visiting on Sunday and a trip to Arsenal next Saturday, they have an extremely unforgiving start.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Olid deserves time and patience. She is well respected and comes with a wealth of experience in her native Spain across boys’ academy football and women’s football and spent time at Houston Dynamo in the US.

Alongside battling critics unimpressed with the state of the team in their opening WSL game or questioning her managerial pedigree, she must contend with wave after wave of appalling sexist comments on social media that greet her every appearance. That surely will take a toll.

If Olid is able to weather the storm of frustration – which will grow if the team falter while players get used to her philosophy – and to force United to loosen the purse strings, they will be huge accomplishments.

Unfortunately, even success on the pitch is unlikely to end the online comments; it will probably just shift their tone. She deserves better in so many ways. The hope will be that she can build a connection with the playing group that enables them to punch above their weight until reinforcements potentially appear in January.

Their first opportunity to fend off the vultures is when they welcome Chelsea to Leigh and, with the Blues unconvincing in the final third against Aston Villa last Saturday, they can have a little hope.

Sports.title: Phil Parkinson’s future questioned as ‘woeful’ Wrexham handed heaviest loss of Hollywood era
Sports.content:
Phil Parkinson has been warned of pressure in the Wrexham hot seat after they were thumped 6-0 by West Ham United.

Jarrod Bowen, Joel Piroe, Konstantinos Mavropanos, Taty Castellanos, Mohamadou Kante and Manor Solomon netted as the Hammers were a class above their visitors.

3 Parkinson watched his Wrexham side ship six goals at West Ham Credit: Getty
